newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tapsell, McLean knighted in NZ New Year honours.
newsitem.headline: Tapsell, McLean knighted in NZ New Year honours.

text.p: WELLINGTON, Dec 31 - Three knights and a dame have been named in the New Year Honours list for 1997, the second honours to be announced under the New Zealand Royal Honours System, NZPA reported.

They are former High Court judge Thomas Thorp, sports journalist Terence (TP or Terry) McLean, former Speaker of Parliament Peter Tapsell -- who all become Knights Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit (KNZM) -- and botanist/researcher Dr Ella Campbell, who becomes a Dame Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit (DNZM).

Under the new honours system the order of precedence is the Order of New Zealand, whose membership is limited to 20 people. It is followed by the Queen's Service Order, the Queen's Service Medal and the new New Zealand Order of Merit, introduced mid-year.
The latter Order of Merit is ranked: Knights and Dames Grand Companion (GNZM), Knights and Dames Companions (KNZM and DNZM), Companions (CNZM), Officers (ONZM) and Members (MNZM).

Retired politicians made Companions of the New Zealand Order of Merit for public service are former Labour trade and industry minister David Caygill, and former National ministers Warren Cooper (defence, local government and internal affairs) and John Falloon (agriculture, forestry and racing).

All Blacks captain and most capped All Black (83 tests) Sean Fitzpatrick is made an Officer of the New Zealand Order of Merit (ONZM), and All Black and Sevens star Zinzan Brooke becomes a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit (MNZM) for their services to rugby.

Swimmers to be recognised with an ONZM are double Olympic gold medallist Danyon Loader who won the 200 and 400 metre freestyle events at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, and Duane Kale who won four gold medals, one silver and one bronze at this year's Paralympics.
Racehorse trainer Eric Ropiha also becomes an ONZM for his services to racing and equestrian sport.
Other sports people to receive MNZMs are All Black Michael Jones, former New Zealand cricket captain Ken Rutherford and former New Zealand rugby league captain Gary Freeman.
